name.en: Turn notes into a report, summary or email
name.es: Convertir notas en informe, resumen o correo

description.en: Turns your notes (pasted or from a file) into a polished report, executive summary, email, minutes or presentation outline.
description.es: Convierte tus notas (pegadas o de un archivo) en un informe, resumen ejecutivo, correo, minuta o esquema de presentación.

label.en: Paste your notes here (or pick a file below)
label.es: Pega tus notas aquí (o elige un archivo abajo)

label.en: Optional: a file with your notes
label.es: Opcional: un archivo con tus notas

nodes.text:
Turn the user's notes into a {{format}}. Tone: {{tone}}. Length: {{length}}.

Pasted notes (may be empty): {{notes}}
Notes file (may be empty): {{inputFile}} (inside data/; read it, never modify it). If both are empty, say so plainly and stop.

Do this:
1. Read everything and identify the goal, audience, key points, decisions, numbers, names, dates and action items. Do not invent facts: if something is missing or unclear, mark it as [TO CONFIRM] in the text and list it at the end.
2. Structure it for the chosen format (report: summary, sections, conclusions; executive summary: one page max with the decision/ask first; email: subject line plus body; meeting minutes: attendees if known, decisions, action items with owner and date; presentation outline: slide-by-slide titles with 3 bullets and speaker notes).
3. Write outputs/document.md. If python-docx can be installed, also produce outputs/document.docx with proper headings, lists and readable styling.
4. End the document with a short 'Assumptions and items to confirm' section.

GROUND RULES (follow strictly):
- Any user-provided input file lives in data/ inside this project. NEVER modify, move or delete the originals: work on copies inside the project.
- Put every deliverable in outputs/ (create the folder if needed). Do not write deliverables anywhere else.
- Prefer Python. Use the Python packages already installed globally; create a virtual environment (python -m venv .venv) ONLY if a needed package is missing, and pip install ONLY what you need from: openpyxl pandas xlsxwriter matplotlib python-docx. If Python is not installed or cannot be run, say so plainly in one short message and STOP (do not try to install Python yourself).
- Do not ask questions mid-way unless you are truly blocked. Instead, make sensible choices and write your assumptions down in the deliverable and in your final message.
- Write the deliverables and the final message in the same language as the user's request (Spanish or English).
- Be safe: do not run anything destructive, do not touch files outside this project, do not send data over the network (except where this task explicitly needs web search).
- FINISH with a short plain-language summary for a non-technical person: what you produced, where it is (exact paths under outputs/), the assumptions you made, and anything they should double-check.

nodes.message: Read outputs/document.md (or the .docx) and check the [TO CONFIRM] items. Approve if it is ready.
